comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C18, C65-C66, C69-C70. Both evaluations support the integrative conclusion that MT polarity instructs subcellular protein distribution and is instructive for neurite identity. Peer reviewers found this of 'potentially high significance' while OpenEval noted it is 'well-supported by combined observations.'

Perfect agreement on claims C5, C40-C41 regarding kinesin-1-NudC cross-linking. Both evaluations express uncertainty due to lack of quantification and missing controls. OpenEval notes absence of kinesin-1-alone controls and polarity demonstration, while peer reviewers note 'quantification is lacking from main Figures 1, 4, and 5.'

Perfect agreement on claims C67-C68 regarding dendrite length and outgrowth. Both evaluations express uncertainty about the dendrite elongation phenotype. OpenEval notes 'limited quantitative data on outgrowth dynamics' while peer reviewers question whether unc-116-MT rescues dendrite elongation and note 'the basis of this phenotype appears complex.'

Disagreement on claims C14-C15, C42-C49 regarding structure-function analysis. OpenEval finds the domain-specific requirements 'well-designed' and supported, while peer reviewers express uncertainty, requesting more accuracy in describing the e2310 allele and questioning whether the C. elegans sequence actually binds MTs.

Agreement on claims C17, C36-C39 regarding dendritic protein localization defects. Both evaluations support these findings showing reduced dendritic localization of ACR-2::GFP and CAM-1::YFP. Peer reviewers requested additional quantification but did not challenge validity of observations.

Agreement on claims C46, C50-C53 regarding KLC independence. Both evaluations support the finding that klc-1; klc-2 double mutants have transport defects but normal MT polarity, demonstrating functional separation. Peer reviewers accepted this as part of the structure-function analysis without raising concerns.

Agreement on claims C54-C56 regarding MT accumulation in dendrites. Both evaluations support the quantitative findings showing increased tubulin intensity and EBP-2 comet frequency. Peer reviewers did not challenge these data, which support the 'sliding out' model, though they questioned other aspects of the mechanism.

Strong disagreement on claims C8-C9 regarding mammalian dendritic MT polarity. OpenEval considers these 'well-established prior knowledge supported by extensive citations,' while peer reviewers explicitly corrected this claim, stating it is 'not correct' and citing multiple papers showing mixed polarity in proximal dendrites and plus-end-out in distal dendrites.

Disagreement on claims C6, C57 regarding the sliding mechanism model. OpenEval supports the 'sliding out' model based on MT accumulation data, while peer reviewers express uncertainty, proposing 'an equally likely interpretation' that kinesin-1 promotes transport of plus-end MTs out of dendrites and questioning how the model prevents MT collapse into the cell body.

Agreement on claims C3-C4, C23-C26, C33 regarding core finding of MT polarity reversal in unc-116 mutants. Both evaluations support this discovery. OpenEval notes 'multiple lines of evidence' while peer reviewers found it 'potentially interesting and novel' and of 'potentially high significance,' though they requested additional quantification.

Agreement on claims C19-C22 regarding baseline MT polarity in wild-type neurons. Both evaluations support these findings from fluorescently tagged motor proteins and EBP-2::GFP imaging. OpenEval notes these provide 'appropriate controls for subsequent mutant analyses' while peer reviewers accepted these as part of the overall discovery.

Agreement on claims C16, C34-C35 regarding mislocalization of synaptic proteins to dendrites. Both evaluations support these findings showing GFP::RAB-3 and mCherry::SYD-2 mislocalization as functional consequences of MT polarity reversal. Peer reviewers requested additional quantification but accepted the observations.

Disagreement on claim C60 regarding prior work on kinesin-2. OpenEval considers this claim (and others C10-C13, C58-C63) as 'accurately represent cited prior work,' while peer reviewers explicitly noted the omission of Mattie et al Curr Biol 2010 showing kinesin-2's role in minus-end-out MT orientation in flies, stating 'The authors should cite this paper and discuss the relevance.'
